refuters.argument:
Not refuted. The row's finite successor model matches the printed convention (sm-3 lines 29-38) and the source proof's own model (sm-3 lines 96-115), and the tiny example behaves exactly as the printed rule requires.

(a) ρ is the traversal successor. Mark P = ZMod n ⊕ Visit P (CarrierMarks.lean:33); markPosition sends vertex i to (i,0) and visit ⟨c,i⟩ to (i, t_ci) with t_ci strictly in (0,1) (CarrierMarks.lean:37-40, GaussVisits.lean:48-52, Crossings.lean:102-111). markKey = i.val + t (Traversal.lean:17, CarrierMarks.lean:79-80), i.e. the lexicographic (edge, parameter) order of def:gauss (sm-1 ~249) linearised with the cut at (0,0). No ties are possible: markKey is injective under Generic (CarrierMarks.lean:89-91), because a vertex (integer key) cannot equal a visit (non-integer key), two visits on one edge with equal parameter would give equal crossing points contradicting generic_crossingPoint_injective (Crossings.lean:113-133), and the two visits of one crossing sit on different (remote) edges. markList = Finset.univ.sort under the lifted linear order (CarrierMarks.lean:99-103), length n+2|X| (line 122-124), nonempty via vertex 0 (line 130-133), so the cycle is nonempty even with no crossings, as the source says (sm-3:98-99). nextMark/prevMark are Cycle.next/prev on that list (CarrierSuccessor.lean:49-54); markSuccessor_getElem shows index i ↦ (i+1) mod length, i.e. the closing wrap from the maximal-key mark back to vertex 0 (lines 93-100). So ρ is the successor of the circle marked at every vertex and visit.

(b) Reconnection. smoothingSuccessor = (selectedMarkPerm S).trans markSuccessor = ρ ∘ σ (CarrierSmoothing.lean:82-84) with σ swapping the two visits of every selected crossing and fixing everything else (CarrierSmoothing.lean:36-38, CarrierVisitTwin.lean:80-81, 103-107). Hence ρ_S(a) = ρ(b), ρ_S(b) = ρ(a) at a selected pair and ρ_S = ρ elsewhere — exactly eq. carrierpr:successors and "at an unselected marked point keep its outgoing arrow" (sm-3:102-107). Statement clauses reconnect_a/reconnect_b (statement lines 34-37), unselected_visit and vertex (lines 48-50) are these facts.

(c) Ownership. The printed rule assigns a to the cycle containing the incoming one-sided arc at a. Under ρ_S the arc arriving at a comes from (ρ_S)⁻¹(a) = σ(ρ⁻¹(a)) (since ρ_S⁻¹ = σ⁻¹∘ρ⁻¹ = σ∘ρ⁻¹), which has the same plane point as ρ⁻¹(a) (selectedMarkPerm_evaluation, CarrierSmoothing.lean:54-62), so geometrically it is the old incoming one-sided arc at a; that arc lies in a's own ρ_S-cycle, and owner a = ⟦a⟧ (CarrierSmoothing.lean:130-132, owner_iff line 59-60 of the statement). This is literally the source's "the node a retains its incoming arc and leaves along the old outgoing arc at b. This also implements the incoming-visit convention explicitly" (sm-3:112-115). The incoming_arc clause (statement lines 42-46) records precisely this identification, for every mark (a harmless strengthening).

(e) same_point (lines 53-55) is the shared crossing point of the two visits; distinct_carriers (lines 56-57) is the only non-definitional content and is where IsDecomposition (independence, DecompositionDefinition.lean:15-17) is needed — it is the presupposition "the two carriers through that smoothing site" of the convention and the splitting argument of the source proof. (f) Domain: generic P, n ≥ 3, S ∈ Ind(G_P), as in def:smoothing (sm-3:14-15); appropriate.

Tiny example (computed): n=4, μ0=(0,0), μ1=(1,0), μ2=(0,1), μ3=(1,1); X(P) = {{1,3}} with t_13 = t_31 = 1/2. Marks in order (keys): V0(0), V1(1), a=(1,1/2)(3/2), V2(2), V3(3), b=(3,1/2)(7/2). ρ: V0→V1→a→V2→V3→b→V0. For S={{1,3}}: ρ_S(a)=ρ(b)=V0, ρ_S(b)=ρ(a)=V2, all else unchanged. Cycles of ρ_S: (V0 V1 a) and (V2 V3 b) — the two triangles μ0μ1x and μ2μ3x of the bowtie. Incoming one-sided arc at a is V1→a (along E_1 from μ1 to x); it lies in (V0 V1 a) = owner(a). Incoming arc at b is V3→b (along E_3 from μ3 to x); it lies in (V2 V3 b) = owner(b). owner(a) ≠ owner(b). Under the opposite (outgoing) rule a would go to (V2 V3 b), so the row's choice is discriminating and is the printed incoming rule. (ρ_S)⁻¹ = σ∘ρ⁻¹ and owner((ρ_S)⁻¹ x) = owner(x) verified for all six marks.

Adopting the source proof's successor model as the definition of carriers and ownership is a faithful reading: the source itself states that the model's cycles "are precisely the oriented reconnections" and that it "implements the incoming-visit convention explicitly", and rem:selected-visits calls the convention a disambiguation only. Nothing printed is missing or vacuous; the row is slightly stronger than the source in stating incoming_arc for every mark and distinct_carriers for every selected visit (both true consequences consistent with the source), and weaker in nothing.

In Mathlib, Equiv.trans e₁ e₂ = ⟨e₂ ∘ e₁, …⟩ (Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Defs.lean:161-162), so ρ_S(a) = ρ(σ_S(a)). selectedMarkPerm S = sumCongr (refl) (selectedVisitTwinPerm S); selectedVisitTwin S v = if v.1 ∈ S then visitTwin v else v; visitTwin v = ⟨same crossing, the other edge index⟩ (visitTwin_ne, visitTwin_unique). Hence for a selected visit a = v with twin b: ρ_S(a) = ρ(b) and ρ_S(b) = ρ(a) — verbatim sm-3:103-105. reconnect_a / reconnect_b in the statement file state exactly these two equations. The opposite composition σ_S∘ρ would redirect the arc arriving at a to land on node b (an outgoing-visit convention); the row's order, confirmed definitionally by smoothingSuccessor_visit_of_mem's `change markSuccessor hn hP (Sum.inr (selectedVisitTwin S v)) = _`, rules that out.

(c) Incoming-arc ownership. Under ρ_S = ρ∘σ_S the predecessor of a is ρ_S⁻¹(a) = σ_S(ρ⁻¹(a)) (σ_S is an involution), which has the same plane point as ρ⁻¹(a) (selectedMarkPerm_evaluation: both visits of one crossing evaluate to crossingPoint). So the straight subsegment traversed by a's own ρ_S-cycle immediately before a is the same plane segment as the original arc (ρ⁻¹(a), a), which by markSuccessor_prev_no_mark_between contains no other mark and is the "oriented straight subsegment" of sm-3:99-100 whose terminal germ is the incoming one-sided arc at a. a then leaves toward ρ(b), the old outgoing arc at b. Therefore the cycle containing the incoming one-sided arc at a IS the ρ_S-cycle through the node a, and owner a := Quotient.mk a in Component = Quotient (SameCycle.setoid ρ_S) is the printed assignment (sm-3:32-34), matching sm-3:113-115 "the node a retains its incoming arc and leaves along the old outgoing arc at b. This also implements the incoming-visit convention explicitly." The outgoing arc at a (a → ρ(a)) is traversed in b's cycle since ρ_S(b) = ρ(a); for independent S that is a different cycle (distinct_carriers), so the row does NOT assign a to the outgoing-arc cycle. Could "owner a = own cycle" disagree with the printed rule? Only if ρ_S were σ_S∘ρ, excluded by (b). The degenerate case ρ⁻¹(a) = b cannot occur (a, b lie on remote edges i ≠ j, so vertex (i+1,0) separates them), and even then the statement's semantics would be unchanged. The incoming_arc clause (∀ a : Mark P) has three conjuncts: ρ_S⁻¹ a = σ_S (ρ⁻¹ a) (pins the composition order), equal plane points of σ_S(ρ⁻¹ a) and ρ⁻¹ a, and owner (ρ_S⁻¹ a) = owner a. The third is true for any permutation (owner_predecessor) — tautological in isolation — but with the first two it is the correct formal rendering of "the cycle containing the incoming arc at a is a's own cycle". Its quantification over all marks (not just selected visits) is true and harmless.

(d) unselected_visit and vertex: ρ_S = ρ at unselected visits and at vertices (sm-3:106 "At an unselected marked point keep its outgoing arrow"). With owner = own cycle, an unselected visit's owner is the cycle carrying both its incident arcs along its edge (ρ_S(v) = ρ(v), and ρ_S⁻¹(v) has the plane point of ρ⁻¹(v)), i.e., ordinary traversal ownership (sm-3:34). Not omitted.

(e) same_point: both visits of a crossing evaluate to crossingPoint (markPosition_evaluation_visit, visitTwin_crossing) — stated for all visits, true. distinct_carriers (selected v: owner v ≠ owner (visitTwin v)) formalizes the presupposition "the two carriers through that smoothing site" (sm-3:35-37) and lem:carriers (i) last sentence (sm-3:70-71). It genuinely needs independence: with two interlaced selected crossings a b a' b' the swaps give one cycle a→b'→a'→b→a.

Omissions checked: "It specifies endpoint ownership only; the geometric reconnection is unchanged" (sm-3:38-39) has no separate clause, but in this model the reconnection is ρ_S, fixed by reconnect_a/b + unselected_visit + vertex in terms of ρ and S alone, and ownership is read off ρ_S's cycles (owner_iff); there is no independent geometric datum the convention could alter, so nothing checkable is missing. rem:selected-visits' "changes no support, turn or retained-crossing datum" is explanatory remark text, not part of the convention.
